subject.title: Feature Request: Add custom client display name for TUI

question: Should OpenClaw expose a user-facing TUI display-name override, and should that surface be CLI-only, persisted config, or automatically derived?
rationale: The implementation seam is clear, but this adds public CLI/config-adjacent behavior and changes Gateway-visible presence metadata, so automation should not choose naming, persistence, or privacy defaults.

options.title: Add CLI-only opt-in flag
options.body: Add a bounded `openclaw tui --client-name <name>` path that affects only this Gateway-mode process and leaves the current default unchanged.

options.title: Add persisted TUI config
options.body: Add a `tui` config key only if maintainers want a stable per-user default, with schema, docs, validation, and upgrade-safe behavior.

options.title: Defer automatic naming
options.body: Keep `openclaw-tui` as the only TUI presence label until a broader TUI identity and privacy policy is decided.

recommendation.title: Add CLI-only opt-in flag
recommendation.body: Add a bounded `openclaw tui --client-name <name>` path that affects only this Gateway-mode process and leaves the current default unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is tied to the current label introduction and is the strongest available routing signal for the public CLI/product decision.
